notes: The colophon is in Hindi (Braj/Bundeli). It closes the Kayāmatnāmā and the Kulajam Sāhab, the Prāṇanāthī/Praṇāmī scripture. Its author Prāṇanātha is not named in the colophon, so he is not listed. The catalogue gives the scribe as Aṃjīradāsa, but the quoted colophon names only paṃ purohita Lalanajū as the writer ('liṣyate'). Aṃjīradāsa may appear elsewhere in the manuscript; this cannot be checked here. The copy was made in the gumaṭī (small shrine or cell) of Bābā Jīvanadāsa at Sāhigaḍha. This is probably Shahgarh (Sagar district, MP), a Praṇāmī area, but the identification is not certain. 'śrīdhanavāī kaunai hai pālakī' is obscure. It may mean the copy was made for, or belongs to, Dhanabāī (a woman's name), so role and confidence are tentative. The era is assumed to be VS, because 'saṃvatu' with kuvāra vadi is the North Indian usage (VS 1909 = 1852 CE, September). The weekday was not verified.
